sql_key (src/sqllens/memory/importer.py:50-64) parses with sqlglot.parse(read='mysql'), drops None entries, and if exactly one statement remains returns ('parsed', stmt.sql(dialect='mysql')). Otherwise (zero or multiple statements, or any Exception including TokenError/RecursionError via the broad except at line 62) it returns ('text', sql.strip()). Hence non-single-statement text matches only identical text modulo leading/trailing whitespace; the tuple tag keeps a text key from colliding with a parsed key. Reformatted single statements regenerate identically; sqlglot generation does not change literal or identifier case (only the optimizer's normalize_identifiers does, and it is not called), so `WHERE region = 'EU'` and `where region = 'eu'` differ in literal while keyword case is normalized. Two-statement input gives len 2 so falls to text. Matches doc claim.

Counterexample for the add tool: admin.add_memories (admin.py:262-294) validates each item first and drops failing ones into per-row errors BEFORE building the bundle passed to import_bundle. A call with one valid pair plus an item such as {question:'', sql:'select 1', groups:['bogus']} (fails SqlPair validation) names an unknown group, yet unknown_groups only sees the valid pairs, so no refusal happens; the valid pair is written and the response is a per-row validation error that does not name the unknown group.
